label: Can shared creatures identify the same ultimate source across alternative histories?
summary: See docs/notes/contingency-receptivity-c2.md#can-ordinary-individuals-identify-the-same-foundation-across-histories. Suppose n sources every originated member of a fixed class wherever n exists, and a creature once originating from n always requires that very n. A finite sequence carries n to the final history if at each step a class member originates in the outgoing history and that very individual exists in the incoming one. The final history may omit all actual creatures. A mixed history of the original individuals under these conditions can connect a seemingly separate population. A solitary source could be identified through a productive extension under a further exclusive-role premise. Biological lineage can identify particular ancestors of a fossil but gives no reason to count a giver of existence as a biological ancestor. Direct creation of a rational soul removes the intermediates but identifies the kind of producer. Aquinas distinguishes the agent’s act from the soul and accounts for the soul’s initial individuation through its body. Neither case settles the creator’s numerical identity across alternatives. If n could produce each numerically particular possible creature in the selected class as its ultimate source and each creature once so produced requires n, even populations that cannot mix must contain n if they contain a class member. Histories lacking such members remain open. Power over every possible kind leaves this singular task open. Necessary emanation, morally required relief and an impure singleton were tested at fixed scope. None supplies both independent modal evidence and the required direction of dependence. Moderate confidence in suspension for the shared C2 profile. Analyst assessment, no formal premise change.
blocker: Proximate origin does not by itself make the ultimate source irreplaceable. Component coverage requires independently admissible joint histories of original individuals and an account of creatureless orders. No tested condition is both guaranteed by this n and independently omissible on a reading compatible with its actual presence. Reopen on evidence for those links or for one invariant content that irreducibly requires n in each alternative.
